authority: This manifest is proposal-stage Evidence only. It is not Approved, not Published, not Effective. It lists every normative valid, invalid and canonical-trace fixture in this change set.

fixtures.focus: First committed root Message with one text part, normal-path success.
Committed assistant Message with structural parent, normal continuation.
Original MessageBranch record after root Message and first assistant reply.
BranchHeadEvent version 1 has no previousHeadMessageId.
BranchHeadEvent version 2 requires previousHeadMessageId referencing the prior head.
headVersion 1 SHALL NOT carry previousHeadMessageId (if/then/else); rejected.
Actor- and device-scoped view state; never carries graph-truth-mutating fields.
Amended sibling Message shares the source's structural parent (REF-042 §9.3).
Amendment derivation relation from the amended sibling back to its source Message.
End-to-end CommitMessageAmendment success: new branch, new head, fresh graph revision.
Exact commandId replay returns the original result with idempotentReplay true (REF042-INV-015).
A result SHALL NOT carry both a successful body and a failure envelope; REF-042 §13.5 requires validation failure to create no Message or branch, i.e. only a Failure, never a partial result.
A commandId reused with different content correctly fails closed as idempotency_conflict (REF042-INV-016).
expectedVersion is a required optimistic-concurrency precondition on ReorderQueuedSubmission; omitting it is rejected as incomplete.
Pinned branch-path reconstruction result at a fixed head and graph revision.
Supplying pinnedHeadMessageId without pinnedGraphRevision is rejected (if/then).
A detected delivery gap yields a stable ResnapshotResponse rather than a guessed continuation.
An unauthorised cursor likewise yields resnapshot, never a guessed continuation.
Structural event published after commit, carrying graphRevision and conversationSequence.
additionalProperties:false rejects an injected raw-content field on a minimised transport event.
An unrecognised but well-formed open MessagePart.type decodes inertly, not rejected.
Share pinned to branch, head and graph revision (REF-042 §18.1).
revokedAt is a well-formed, readable field; re-authorisation at read time (not schema shape) is what actually denies access to a revoked share (REF042-RULE-019).
selected_branch_snapshot export constrained to exactly one BranchSnapshotRef.
selected_branch_snapshot scope is constrained to exactly one BranchSnapshotRef by if/then; two is rejected.
A valid Attachment Reference revalidation carries no failure field.
A revoked attachment revalidates to outcome invalid with a structured failure, blocking amendment commit (REF042-INV-017/ADR022-INV-013).
outcome invalid requires a failure body (if/then); omitting it is rejected.
GenerationJob reaching succeeded state with a linked resultMessageId.
F2a request carries only opaque connection/model references, structured messages and an absolute deadline.
ProviderModelId permits a real namespaced provider/adapter model identity (openai/gpt-4.1), which WorkspaceScopedId's no-`/` shape could not.
ProviderModelId rejects a raw URL (the `://` scheme marker) masquerading as a model identity.
additionalProperties:false rejects an injected credential field on the F2a request boundary.
additionalProperties:false rejects injected arbitrary URL and header fields.
additionalProperties:false rejects an injected raw prompt string.
additionalProperties:false rejects a leaked policy-internal trace field on the terminal ErrorEvent.
additionalProperties:false rejects an out-of-band mutation marker on a committed Message.
additionalProperties:false rejects an out-of-band parent-override field; parentMessageId itself is immutable post-commit and no schema field exists to bypass that (ADR022-INV-002).

sourceMessageId equal to derivedMessageId is a self-cycle, forbidden by REF-042 §7.4 acyclicity (REF042-INV-004); detected by the validator's acyclicity check since JSON Schema cannot compare two dynamic sibling fields for inequality.

A Message asserting a workspaceId different from the trusted, server-supplied session context is rejected at the authorisation boundary (REF042-RULE-001, REF042-RULE-012); the schema shape alone is valid, so this is proven by the validator's workspace-scope relational check.

A child Message naming a parentMessageId from a different Conversation than its own conversationId violates REF042-RULE-004 (parent writes rejected when they would create a cross-Conversation link); proven by the validator's cross-conversation relational check.
An amendment derivation whose source Message is assistant-authored violates REF042-INV-008 (amendment source and derived must both be user-role); proven by the validator's role-pair check.
F2a canonical trace class 1: text-only success terminating in finish(stop) with provider-reported usage.
F2a canonical trace class 2: multi-part text/reasoning lifecycle; reasoning events carry no content field.
F2a canonical trace class 3: the provider reuses toolCallId tool-XYZ across step-1 and step-2; disambiguated by (attemptId, stepId, toolCallId) per CHAT-RUNTIME-CONTRACT-V1-FREEZE.md §11 rule 4.
F2a canonical trace class 4: clean caller-initiated cancellation terminates via finish(finishReason=cancelled).
F2a canonical trace class 5: absolute deadline exceeded terminates via error(timeout, retryable=true).
F2a canonical trace class 6: three independent attempts, one per error class (authentication, rate-limited, endpoint-policy), each terminating cleanly via error.
F2a canonical trace class 7: the stream ends with no finish or error event, classified malformed-response (CHAT-RUNTIME-CONTRACT-V1-FREEZE.md §11 rule 1).

F2a canonical trace class 8: a duplicate providerEventId at ordinal 2/3 (consumer dedupes by providerEventId) and a duplicate finish at ordinal 5/6, which is a protocol violation (CHAT-RUNTIME-CONTRACT-V1-FREEZE.md §11 rule 2).

F2a canonical trace class 9: an unrecognised additive eventType (`video-frame`, not in the closed v1 ProviderEventType set) fails strict v1 validation at that item, which is precisely the trigger a real consumer uses to apply the safe-diagnostic/resnapshot policy (freeze §11 rule 6), not a contradiction of that policy.

F2a canonical trace class 10: attempt-t10a fails transport/retryable, attempt-t10b retries under the SAME invocationId and route and succeeds with no routeEvidence, because no route change occurred — a same-route retry never needs, and never silently claims, a fallback.
F2a canonical trace class 11: an explicit, authorized fallback carries RouteEvidence naming both the configured and the resolved route on its terminal event (freeze §11 rule 7).
The resolved route differs from the configured route but the terminal finish event carries no RouteEvidence: an undeclared, silent fallback, denied by the route-evidence check (freeze §11 rule 7).

routeDecision configured is claimed even though admittedRoute differs from configuredPreference: a changed route may not be labelled configured (freeze §11 rule 7); caught by route_evidence_internally_consistent since JSON Schema cannot compare two nested sibling objects for equality.
Host-issued admission handshake declaring bounded message/batch/item size and F2b's own independent bridgeProtocolVersion (F2b freeze §12.0-§12.2).
Terminal lifecycle message for one hosted renderer instance (F2b freeze §12.3).
One final snapshot page (hasMore false) carrying snapshotId/snapshotGraphRevision/pageIndex and the snapshotBoundaryCursor a subsequent event-batch continues from.
One bounded, ordered batch of Chat transport events continuing from the frozen snapshot boundary via fromCursor.
Host-mediated command whose payload validates against the exact D07 SubmitMessageRequest schema its commandKind names.
Carries the exact D07 CommandResultEnvelope with status accepted, never an invented outcome vocabulary.
D07's own CommandResultEnvelope if/then/else forbids error when status is accepted; carried through the bridge unchanged, still rejected.
Carries the exact D07 CommandResultEnvelope with status rejected and a required error.
reason forbidden_capability requires deniedCapability to be present (if/then); omitting it is rejected.
Instructs the hosted renderer to discard local state and request a fresh snapshot via an explicit bridge.snapshot-request, never a renderer-side fetch.
Module->host pause carrying the required bounded pendingEvents count and watermarkCursor acknowledgement.
A command bearing a contextId other than the bound one is immediately refused as context_mismatch (F2b freeze §12.1, §12.4).
A context-mismatched command with no following refusal is a protocol violation, caught by the validator's context-mismatch relational check.
A command received after bridge.context-disposed is refused as late_command, never queued and replayed against a new context (F2b freeze §12.3, §12.6).
A late command with no following refusal after disposal is a protocol violation, caught by the validator's late-command relational check.
No event-batch is sent between a pause and its matching resume (F2b freeze §12.8).
An event-batch sent while paused, with no intervening resume, is a protocol violation (F2b freeze §12.8).

The same eventId is delivered twice (at-least-once transport). A consumer dedupes by eventId (freeze §9 rule 2); presence of an undeduplicated repeat in a recorded consumer log is exactly the condition the duplicate-event check catches.
Supplying pinnedGraphRevision without pinnedHeadMessageId is likewise rejected (allOf, symmetric direction of the pinned-snapshot invariant).
Provider event ordinals are strictly increasing per attempt; a duplicate ordinal (not merely a descending one) is rejected.
The stable CommandResultEnvelope with status accepted and no error.
The stable CommandResultEnvelope with status completed and an optional resultRef.
The stable CommandResultEnvelope with status rejected and a required safe error.
The stable CommandResultEnvelope with status conflict and an optional currentVersion, no error.
status rejected requires error (if/then); omitting it is rejected.
status accepted SHALL NOT carry error; rejected.
status conflict MAY carry both an optional stable error and an optional currentVersion together.
currentVersion uses the generic bounded non-negative ResourceVersion type; a negative value is rejected.
error.code must be a member of the shared ErrorCode registry, not an arbitrary string.
ProviderInvocationRequest.operation is fixed to the const language.stream; any other value is rejected.
A complete F2a request exercising generationOptions, providerOptions and an optional causationId.
ProviderOptionsNamespaceValue's BoundedExtensiblePropertyName denylist rejects a reserved credential-shaped key (apiKey) before adapter invocation.
SanitisedScalarValue's number branch is itself finitely bounded (±1,000,000,000); a value past that ceiling satisfies no anyOf branch.
The Gate-B launch boundary requires policyRef; omitting it is rejected.
ProviderMessagePart.kind text permits only text; a tool-call field on a text part is rejected.
ResponseFormat.schemaRef is forbidden unless kind is structured; present on a text format is rejected.
ToolInputLifecycleEvent.toolName is required on tool-input-start; omitting it is rejected.
SourceEvent requires at least evidenceReference or displayLabel; carrying neither is rejected.
A SourceEvent carrying only displayLabel (no evidenceReference) satisfies the anyOf invariant.
An empty displayLabel cannot satisfy the at-least-one-source-identity anyOf rule; minLength:1 rejects it.
A non-terminal ProviderInvocationRecord carries neither terminalAt nor routeEvidence.
A newly requested ProviderInvocationRecord may have zero Attempts (none admitted yet); attemptIds:[] is permitted only for lifecycleState requested.

A terminal ProviderInvocationRecord requires terminalAt and a complete routeEvidence; routeDecision configured with admittedRoute naming the identical connectionId/modelId (plus required adapter fields configuredPreference never carries) is relationally consistent.

A terminal ProviderInvocationRecord with routeDecision same_route_retry and an admittedRoute naming the identical connectionId/modelId as configuredPreference is relationally consistent (positive same-route-retry case).
A terminal lifecycleState (succeeded) with attemptIds:[] is rejected: only a newly requested invocation may have zero Attempts.
attemptIds carrying the same ProviderAttemptId twice violates uniqueItems.
A terminal lifecycleState (succeeded) without terminalAt/routeEvidence is rejected (if/then).

A terminal ProviderInvocationRecord's own routeEvidence names a changed admittedRoute connectionId/modelId but is labelled routeDecision configured: a durable record cannot evade the relational invariant that only F2a event-trace wrappers previously checked.
BridgeSnapshotItem itemKind message maps its payload to graph.schema.json#/$defs/Message.
BridgeSnapshotItem itemKind message_branch maps its payload to branch.schema.json#/$defs/MessageBranch.
BridgeSnapshotItem itemKind view_state maps its payload to viewstate.schema.json#/$defs/ConversationViewState.
BridgeSnapshotItem itemKind generation_job maps its payload to generation.schema.json#/$defs/GenerationJob.
itemKind conversation with a Message-shaped payload is rejected: BridgeSnapshotItem enforces the itemKind/payload mapping, not merely an opaque object.
An arbitrary junk payload for itemKind conversation is rejected against the real Conversation schema.
EventBatchMessage.events.items $refs the closed ChatEvent union; an arbitrary, unrecognised item is rejected rather than passed through as an opaque object.
action resume forbids pendingEvents (and watermarkCursor); carrying pendingEvents on a resume is rejected.

An envelope whose declared bounds are all in range but whose actual UTF-8 JSON encoding exceeds 65536 bytes is refused, never truncated: the carrier bound is measured on encoded bytes, not on a declared field.
A kind outside the ten frozen F2b carrier kinds is rejected by the closed enum, mirroring Platform's contract-unknown-kind refusal.
An unsupported outer Platform envelope version (v 2.0) is rejected; the outer carrier version is a separate axis from the F2b bridge protocol version and is pinned independently.
A module-only kind (module/chat.command) sent as host->module is rejected: each carrier kind is bound to its exact direction, mirroring Platform's contract-unknown-direction refusal.
The D07 request payload's workspaceId claim must match the bound context's own workspaceId; a cross-context mismatch is rejected relationally (F2b freeze §12.9).
CreateConversationShare is deferred until Gate F CHAT-029 and is not a member of the closed first-horizon HostedCommandKind allowlist; rejected by enum.
payload.commandId must equal the bridge command's own commandId; a mismatch is rejected relationally since JSON Schema cannot compare two sibling fields for equality.
commandKind SubmitMessage binds payload to the exact SubmitMessageRequest schema; a RenameConversation-shaped payload is missing SubmitMessageRequest's required fields and is rejected.
bridgeProtocolVersion follows the closed major.minor pattern; a malformed value (missing minor) is rejected.
maxMessageBytes is bounded to 61440 (60 KiB), provably encodable inside the evidenced Platform 64 KiB outer carrier; a declared bound above that maximum is rejected.
The supported bridge protocol version is the exact constant 1.0, not merely a major.minor syntax: an unsupported major (2.0) is rejected structurally, never silently downgraded.
A version mismatch within the supported major (1.1) is rejected too: the bundle supports exactly 1.0 and never guesses which additive fields an unknown minor added.
safeMessage is keyed by reason as enforcement, not prose: an oversize refusal carrying the context_disposed copy is rejected by the reason->safeMessage const binding.
fixtures.expected_error_contains: This message is too large to send.

fixtures.focus: A command arriving before any bridge.context-bound admission is refused as context_mismatch: pre-bind traffic fails closed exactly like a genuine mismatch (F2b freeze §12.0.1).
A second bridge.context-bound for a context already bound, with no intervening disposal, is a duplicate bind and a protocol violation, never a silent rebind.

A full session lifecycle: host-mediated snapshot-request, a two-page snapshot with stable snapshotId/pageIndex continuity, an event-batch continuing exactly from the frozen snapshotBoundaryCursor, a command/result round trip and clean disposal.

An event-batch whose fromCursor does not continue from the last known position is a cursor gap; it is immediately followed by bridge.resnapshot and a matching bridge.snapshot-request, never a guessed continuation.
A cursor gap with no following resnapshot is a protocol violation.
A bridge.resnapshot with no following bridge.snapshot-request carrying its exact resnapshotCursor is a protocol violation: the resnapshot request/required flow was not honoured.

A pendingEvents count at or beyond the overflow threshold is answered with bridge.resnapshot (backpressure_overflow), terminating and restarting the subscription rather than accumulating unbounded pending state.
An overflowing pendingEvents count answered with a plain resume instead of a backpressure_overflow resnapshot is a protocol violation.
An event carried in a bridge.event-batch whose workspaceId differs from the bound context's workspaceId is a cross-context leak, caught relationally (F2b freeze §12.9).
The same eventId delivered in two different bridge.event-batch messages is a duplicate, never a new fact.
The host sending a bridge.event-batch for a context after disposing it is a dispose-cleanup violation, distinct from and broader than late-command refusal (host-issued, not module-issued, traffic).
A command sent after bind but before the module opened its snapshot handshake is refused with the precise closed lifecycle reason not_ready, then the handshake proceeds normally.
Pre-ready module traffic silently processed instead of refused not_ready is a protocol violation.
A second page of one snapshot generation carrying a different snapshotId is identity drift, never a silently accepted new generation.
A second page of one snapshot generation carrying a different snapshotGraphRevision is revision drift: the generation is no longer pinned at one structural boundary.
pageIndex must increment by exactly one per page; a 0 -> 2 jump is a page-index discontinuity and a silently dropped page.
A continuation snapshot-request must echo the exact nextCursor the preceding hasMore page issued; a guessed cursor is rejected.
Boundary case: pendingEvents exactly at the frozen overflow threshold (1000) is answered with a backpressure_overflow resnapshot, proving the comparison is at-or-above, not strictly above.
Boundary case: pendingEvents one below the frozen overflow threshold (999) is a normal pause/resume with a valid watermark, proving the threshold does not fire early.
A pause whose watermarkCursor names an earlier position the module has already passed is a stale acknowledgement and is rejected.
A pause whose watermarkCursor names a position the host never issued is a future or unknown acknowledgement and is rejected.
A page of 3 items is well under the global maxItems of 25 but above this bound context's negotiated maxSnapshotItems of 2, and is rejected relationally.
A batch of 3 events is well under the global maxItems of 25 but above this bound context's negotiated maxBatchEvents of 2, and is rejected relationally.
A message far below the 61440-byte global bound but above this bound context's negotiated maxMessageBytes is rejected on its actual UTF-8 encoded size.
Host event delivery in state bound_not_ready, before the module has asked for anything, is a pre-ready protocol violation no refusal can cure.
A clean resume carries neither pendingEvents nor watermarkCursor.
A module->host Platform carrier envelope: exactly v/dir/kind/payload, kind module/chat.command bound to its exact direction and to BridgeCommandMessage, within the 65536-byte encoded carrier bound.
A host->module Platform carrier envelope: kind host/chat.snapshot-page bound to its exact direction and to SnapshotPageMessage, within the 65536-byte encoded carrier bound.
D07 conflict semantics are preserved unchanged through the bridge: status conflict with an optional currentVersion.
A bridge-transport command timeout is refused as bridge lifecycle (command_timeout), never a fifth BridgeCommandResultMessage.result.status value.
A hosted command payload structurally cannot carry a credential; forbidden_capability/credential_direct refusal with a closed, non-reflective safeMessage.
Pre-ready module traffic is refused with the precise closed lifecycle reason not_ready and that reason's single mapped safeMessage.
Module->host request for the first snapshot page of a fresh initial snapshot (no cursor).
Module->host request continuing a resnapshot, carrying the exact resnapshotCursor a prior bridge.resnapshot named.

One live in-flight text delta for an in-progress Generation Attempt: job-scoped (generationEventSequence, no graph revision), minimised, carrying only the governed identity, ordering and delta fields.
chunkOrdinal and textDelta are required; a delta event that names neither is rejected rather than treated as an empty append.
textDelta minLength:1 rejects an empty append, which would advance the stream without carrying text.
textDelta maxLength:262144 rejects an oversized delta at the contract bound; runtime additionally enforces the stricter cumulative UTF-8 byte bound.
eventType const 'chat.generation.text_appended' rejects a document carrying another chat.generation.* discriminator, so the closed branch cannot be reached by the wrong event type.
additionalProperties:false rejects an injected Provider credential field; a minimised live delta admits no endpoint, model, header, credential, raw body or arbitrary metadata.
